introHeading: Editorial portraits for The Bronx's biggest and smallest guest lists alike
introParas: Bronx weddings and Sweet Sixteens tend to bring guest lists that dressed for the occasion, and the glam booth is built to match that effort. Our studio lighting rig renders every guest's skin tone evenly no matter how many people have come through before them, and unlimited prints and digital copies mean nobody at a two-hundred-guest Throggs Neck reception gets turned away because the count ran long.

It pairs naturally with the mirror booth at bigger Bronx events — when a catering hall's guest list is large enough that one line would run all night, adding the glam booth as a second station or pairing it with a roaming attendant keeps both moving. Riverdale's smaller, more design-conscious estate events bring a different flavor: the black-and-white look reads as intentionally editorial rather than just formal, which suits the aesthetic those venues tend to want.

Setup wants 10ft x 10ft for the backdrop and prop table, compressing to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance for tighter halls, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet — we bring our own dedicated power run since many Bronx catering halls run tight circuits for the DJ and kitchen already. Whether the venue sits in Mott Haven or Country Club, The Bronx is a standard service area with no surprise travel fees, quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Glam Photo Booth in The Bronx — FAQ

faqs.q: Can the glam booth keep up with a large Throggs Neck catering-hall wedding?
faqs.a: Yes — unlimited sessions and unlimited prints mean guest count isn't a limit. For very large weddings we often suggest pairing the glam booth with a roaming attendant or a second station so the line stays short through cocktail hour.

faqs.q: How much space does the glam booth need at a Bronx catering hall?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is optimal for the backdrop, prop table and a red-carpet feel; we can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for tighter rooms.

faqs.q: Is color available, or is it black-and-white only?
faqs.a: Both — the black-and-white glam edit is the signature look, but the booth can output color, black-and-white, or let each guest choose.

faqs.q: What power do you need at a Bronx venue?
faqs.a: A standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet of the booth. Because many Bronx catering halls run tight circuits for their own DJ and kitchen equipment, we bring our own dedicated power run.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee to The Bronx?
faqs.a: No surprise fees. The Bronx is a standard service area and we quote travel from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Is the skin-smoothing retouch too strong, or can we tone it down?
faqs.a: It's fully adjustable — we can push it toward a full editorial look or keep it subtle so guests still look like themselves. Tell us your preference before the event.

faqs.q: Can you send a certificate of insurance for a Bronx catering hall that requires one?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy — reply to your booking confirmation with the venue's contact and we will send it over.

faqs.q: Is the glam booth a fit for a Riverdale or Mott Haven design-forward event?
faqs.a: Yes — the black-and-white editorial look works especially well at Riverdale's more private estate events and the newer gallery and loft spaces that have opened up in Mott Haven.

faqs.q: Would the glam booth work for a Bronx quinceañera?
faqs.a: Yes. It's a popular choice for the editorial, red-carpet feel that a quinceañera court often wants — the studio lighting flatters the honoree and every generation of guests equally, and prints can be designed around her colors and theme.

faqs.q: Can the glam booth work at a Country Club or Pelham Bay backyard celebration, not just a catering hall?
faqs.a: Yes. Country Club and the residential streets around Pelham Bay bring us plenty of backyard and small-space bookings, and the glam booth's 8ft x 8ft minimum footprint works fine there — we'll just confirm your power access ahead of time since it's less standardized than a hall's dedicated event floor.
